title: Influence of a dietary intervention and nutritional advice on the inflammatory cytokine pattern as well as clinical disease activity and quality of life of psoriasis patients with loss of effectiveness of biologic therapy
summary:
Previous data show a clear correlation between the concentration of free fatty acids in the blood and the severity of symptom manifestation in patients with psoriasis. Furthermore, it is repeatedly observed in clinical practice that the efficacy of biologic therapy decreases or even gets lost in overweight patients.

So far, it has not been investigated whether a reduction in the concentration of free fatty acids can mitigate this loss of efficacy. We aim to determine whether a dietary intervention, including nutritional counseling, can influence the loss of efficacy of biologic therapy in patients with psoriasis. Additionally, we want to investigate the relationship between psoriasis disease activity and the concentration of various blood values (such as fatty acids in the serum) under a dietary intervention, including nutritional counseling.

Patients who have experienced a loss of efficacy after an initial response to biologic therapy will be recruited for this purpose. In addition to continuing the current psoriasis therapy, a dietary measure with a special formula diet, including nutritional counseling, is planned.

Patients will be clinically examined, the skin condition will be assessed, and blood values will be analyzed. Regular nutritional counseling will also be provided. The study period extends over a total of 5 appointments over a period of 13 weeks.

interventions.name: Formula diet with Almased and nutritional advice for 12 weeks

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Under ongoing biologic therapy PASI 75, then a drop below this value, or
- DLQI decrease by 5 points, or
- PASI initially below 5 under biologic therapy, then a subsequent increase.
Exclusion criteria:
Pregnancy
incompliance
changes in therapy
